claims.text: Sufficient Al addition to CrFeCoNi produces a coherent (Cr,Al)-rich oxide scale.
A coherent (Cr,Al)-rich scale is stable, slow-growing, and adherent above 900 °C.
The (Cr,Al)-rich scale prevents oxide cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNi-based alloys lacking the proposed Al-dependent criterion form mechanically unstable, rapidly growing oxides prone to delamination.
Solution annealing the Al-bearing and Mn-substituted alloys will produce uniform, largely single-phase microstructures.
In-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction can track oxide formation and identify oxide phases in CrMnFeCoNi during high-temperature oxidation.
The proposed diffraction and microscopy measurements can determine oxide composition, interfacial structure, and residual stress throughout exposure.
The controlled exposure will use 1 atm O2 at 900–1000 °C for up to 100 hours.
Low oxide/substrate mismatch strain limits crack initiation and propagation during thermal exposure.
Selective Al and Cr enrichment during exposure produces a stable chromia–alumina-based oxide.
Lattice-parameter matching between the oxide and substrate reduces internal stress.
Reduced oxide growth rate and internal stress prevent cracking and spallation under thermal and corrosive loading.
The Al-bearing alloy will form a slow-growing protective scale that remains intact during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The Mn-substituted variant will form a spinel-based oxide.
The Mn-containing spinel scale will be more susceptible to mismatch-driven cracking and early spallation.
A previously studied lower-Al CrFeCoNi baseline is known to form spinel-like oxides that grow faster and crack under comparable conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to largely single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys with X equal to Si, Mn, or Al at or above 900 °C in oxidizing or corrosive atmospheres.
The exact Al concentration and processing conditions required to form a stable (Cr,Al)-rich scale are not characterized.
Second phases and minor alloying additions may alter oxidation kinetics and scale integrity.
